subject: Token economics & model support — hosted API pricing
summary: Prospect asked for standard per-1M input/output hosted rates, model compatibility, and volume discount bands. Sales provided baseline IO rates, model roster for hosted API, and a starter discount schedule; SE shared the formal ratecard and next steps for procurement.
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@novahealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novahealth.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Token economics & model support — quick ask

Hi Karthik,

We’re kicking off an evaluation of hosted inference vendors and I wanted a quick baseline from Redwood on two things: 1) standard per-1M token pricing (input vs output) for your hosted API, and 2) which hosted models you expose (and their recommended use-cases).

High level context: NovaHealth plans to use an LLM for clinical summarization + patient-facing chat. Initial pilot expected ~10-20M tokens/month, with potential to scale if quality/latency are good.

Specific Qs:
- List of hosted models you support and any guidance (e.g., 13B vs 70B for summarization/chat).
- Baseline IO pricing per 1M tokens (input vs output) for each model class.
- Any standard volume discounts or committed-rate programs for hosted customers.
- Minimum commit or term, and whether dedicated capacity is required for low-latency SLAs.

If easier, a short rate sheet would be great. We’re trying to get procurement a baseline by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Product
NovaHealth

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena@novahealth.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Token economics & model support — hosted API pricing

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the context 94 helpful. I’ll summarize a concise baseline below and attach our short ratecard + SLA summary for procurement. Quick note: the hosted prices below are our standard public starting points; we typically layer in volume-based discounts or committed-capacity pricing for larger pilots. If you can share expected monthly token mix (ratio of generation vs prompts), we’ll tailor the bands.

Baseline hosted API pricing (per 1M tokens) 97 standard, no-commit:
- Redwood-Base-13B (good general purpose / summarization): input $5.00; output $7.25
- Redwood-Opt-33B (preferred for chat/long-context): input $8.50; output $11.50
- Redwood-Long-70B (best for complex reasoning / long-context summaries): input $17.00; output $23.00
- Embeddings endpoint (per 1M vectors processed): $12.00

Hosted model roster (common hosted variants):
- Redwood-Base-13B: efficient summarization, low cost
- Redwood-Opt-33B: balanced latency / quality for chat-style agents
- Redwood-Long-70B: high-quality generation and long-context workflows
- Quantized variants: lower-cost options (if you can tolerate a small quality delta)
- Safety-filtered endpoints and latency-optimized endpoints available (region-specific)

Volume discounts (starter bands, hosted API):
- 0 95 50M tokens/mo: standard rates above
- 50M 95 200M tokens/mo: 10% off list rates
- 200M+ tokens/mo: 20% off list rates (or custom dedicated pricing conversation)

Minimums & SLAs:
- No minimum for hosted API usage. Dedicated capacity / Reserved pools are recommended for strict latency SLOs and guaranteed throughput and typically require a monthly commit.

I’ve attached a short ratecard (Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_v1.pdf) and an SLA summary. I’ll bring Marissa (SE) into the thread to share latency profiles and recommended model for clinical summarization.

Would you have 30 minutes this week for a quick call to go through expected token mix and preferred latency? I can have a tailored proposal ready.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Token economics & model support — hosted API pricing

Marissa / Laura,

Forwarding Elena’s request. Quick asks: can you confirm the latency P50/P95 numbers for the Redwood-Opt-33B and Redwood-Long-70B on hosted (us-west region) at pilot loads (~10-20rps, typical prompt sizes)? Also confirm whether we should push quantized-33B as a cost-savings option for their pilot.

Thanks,
Karthik

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Token economics & model support — hosted API pricing

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the note and the context. Quick responses and next steps below, plus attached files (Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_v1.pdf, SLA_Summary.pdf).

Latency notes (hosted, us-west):
- Redwood-Opt-33B: P50 ~ 70ms per token; P95 ~ 240ms per token at 10-20 rps with continuous batching enabled.
- Redwood-Long-70B: P50 ~ 140ms per token; P95 ~ 420ms per token at similar loads.
- Quantized variants typically reduce cost by ~30% with modest P95 improvements but may increase variance for complex completions.

Discounts/commit guidance:
- We can apply the starter bands Karthik listed. For pilots we often do a 60-day trial credit and then convert to a month-to-month hosted plan; if NovaHealth wants committed discounted rates we can structure a 12-month reserved capacity agreement (Dedicated) with guaranteed throughput and stronger SLA credits.

Attachments & links:
- Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_v1.pdf (baseline list rates and IO breakdown)
- SLA_Summary.pdf
- HubSpot proposal draft: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Next steps:
1) If acceptable, pick a 30-minute slot this week and we’ll walk through token mix assumptions and a tailored discount schedule.
2) Procurement can review the attached PDFs; we can provide a DocuSign if you prefer the standard MSA + SOW path.

Scheduling: https://calendly.com/karthik-redwood/30min

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
